text: A bale and a bend, and a bowl that wants lofting. {lead} swings and sends it up over the hedge in one long arc. It lands by Blackberries.
The wheel has been here since last spring's chase. {lead} sets it rolling, and underneath is a few coins.
A flat stone and a still stretch of water. {lead} sends it dancing across, once, twice, five times, and something on the far side wobbles loose: a purse, a bit damp.
A wall with a tooth missing. {lead} rebuilds it with no mortar and a great deal of dignity, and finds some loose change and a gratitude card in the hollow.
A bale and a bend, and a bowl that wants lofting. {lead} swings and sends it up over the hedge in one long arc. It lands by Brewery Ashtray.
Soft ground, a patient creature, and a lot of worms. {lead} brings up the lot, and under them: Gallopers Horse.
{lead} peers into the water, then pulls out, with great ceremony, Seaweed.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Burn Water Flask.
The old trunk is hollow and ready to go. {lead} heaves, it topples, and out of the hollow rolls Honeycomb.
A glint under the surface, just out of reach. {lead} hooks it with patience and a bit of reed. It is Sea Glass.
{lead} skims a stone over the pool and a bottle on a post tips over. Hanging from it: Burn Water Flask.
Ripples run out from {lead}'s throw like a good rumour, and the stone raps a reed stem. Something drops out of it: Sea Glass.
A glint under the surface, just out of reach. {lead} hooks it with patience and a bit of reed. It is Perch.
A molehill, freshly heaped. {lead} drums a gentle rhythm on the ground and the worms come up to see what the fuss is. Among the soil: Four-Leaf Clover.
A peat pool, black as tea. {lead} dives in, flippers going, and comes up spluttering and delighted with a purse, a bit damp.
A dead trunk, leaning on nothing much. {lead} puts its shoulder to it and over it goes with a crack. Underneath: a purse, a bit damp.
The little round boat wobbles, then settles. {lead} crosses the water with short, careful strokes and lands among the reeds. There is Fresnel Prism.
A knot of sheep, all facing the wrong way. {lead} works them in a neat curve until the gate is clear. Left on the post for you: Double Gloucester.
A gap in the wall, where the stones have gone for a walk. {lead} fits them back one by one, like a very slow jigsaw. Tucked in the wall behind: some loose change and a gratitude card.
A glint under the surface, just out of reach. {lead} hooks it with patience and a bit of reed. It is a few coins.
{lead} skims a flat stone and it ticks off a row of stepping stones, each one settling a little. You hop after it, dry as a bone, mostly.
You hop back along the stepping stones. {lead} skims a stone ahead of you for luck, and it lands every time.
